biography.plain_text: Glenn Straub is an American industrialist and property developer based in Florida. He and his brother inherited their father's automotive businesses before building a fortune in asphalt, concrete and other construction materials. His later acquisitions included distressed properties and Palm Beach Polo, where he became a principal shareholder in the development company.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Palm Beach Polo, Glenn Straub used contracts to encourage homebuilding and discourage speculation in vacant lots. Buyers had to begin construction within two years, while resale before a house was completed could trigger the developer's right to repurchase. The arrangement linked the sale of land to its eventual residential use.

His purchase of Miami Arena in 2004 followed a different course. He reopened the venue for concerts and planned to renovate it, but the older building struggled to compete with newer arenas. He subsequently had it demolished in 2008, leaving the downtown site cleared for redevelopment.
